t: Sum of Beauty of All Substrings with Running Frequencies
o: Beauty of a string is max character frequency minus min frequency among characters PRESENT in it; single-letter substrings score 0. We must sum beauty over all substrings of s - roughly n^2/2 = 125k of them at n = 500. Only 26 lowercase letters exist, so maintaining a 26-slot frequency table per substring is cheap. Example 1: five substrings ("aab", "aabc", "aabcb", "abcb", "bcb") each contribute 1, totaling 5. Example 2 sums to 17. An O(26 * n^2) double loop - about 6.5M elementary steps - fits easily in limits.
k: The minimum frequency must ignore zeros - only letters occurring inside the substring count.
Extending a substring by one character updates frequencies incrementally; never recount from scratch.
n <= 500 legitimizes quadratic enumeration; smarter methods fight for marginal constants.

a.n: Approach 1: Fix Start, Extend End with Running Counts
a.i: Fix the left endpoint i and grow the right endpoint j outward, updating freq[26] incrementally. After each extension, a single 26-slot pass extracts the max and the nonzero min, contributing their difference to the answer. Each substring is processed exactly once per start position.
s: For each start i, reset freq[26].
For each end j >= i, increment freq[s[j]] and scan 26 slots for mx and mn (> 0).
a.t: O(26*n^2) - n^2 extensions, each followed by a 26-slot scan

a.i: Precompute pre[c][i] = occurrences of letter c in the first i characters. The frequency of any letter in s[i..j] is then a single subtraction, enabling arbitrary substring queries without incremental state - useful if substrings were queried in arbitrary order or ranges were reused across computations. Time stays O(26 * n^2); space grows to O(26 * n).
s: Build prefix counts pre[c][i] for all 26 letters.
For each pair (i, j), derive each letter count as pre[c][j+1] - pre[c][i].
Track mx and nonzero mn over the 26 differences.
Add mx - mn to the answer for every pair.
a.t: O(26*n^2) - 26 subtractions per substring after O(26*n) preprocessing

w: Present approach 1 in interviews; bring up prefix sums only if asked about repeated or out-of-order range queries. Pitfalls: letting zero-frequency letters into the min (would wrongly yield beauty 0 everywhere), remembering length-1 substrings contribute 0 automatically (max equals min), and overflow in fixed-width languages for longer alphabets or lengths (fits int comfortably here: at most 26 * 500^2 / 2). Follow-ups: alphabet of size k scales the inner scan to k; counting only substrings whose beauty exceeds a threshold adds an early skip.
